models.title: Reading · Nine years later, the Roadster (finally) flies

block.label: READING · NINE YEARS LATER, THE ROADSTER (FINALLY) FLIES
block.html:
Yesterday, October 15, Tesla unveiled the new Roadster at a SpaceX test facility in Texas. Elon Musk had first shown the car in November 2017, and he had promised that production would start in 2020. Since then, the project had been delayed at least six times, and Tesla had changed the reveal date again and again. In fact, an event planned for October 1 had been cancelled at the last minute due to the weather.

The show was worth the wait, though. In the main stunt, the car drove up a ramp that curled upside down, flew off the end, rolled 180 degrees in the air and landed on its wheels. "Flying cars are real," Musk said, although he also admitted that success "is not guaranteed". The flying version uses high-pressure air tanks, and it isn't approved for public roads.

Back in 2017, buyers had paid $50,000 (or $250,000 for the Founders Series) to reserve a car, and nobody has received one yet. Now, customers can pay a $5,000 deposit for the regular version, whereas the "Rocket" version with the full flight system is invitation only. Tesla hasn't announced a price, and production is planned for 2028. Analysts say the car won't sell in large numbers; however, it puts a spotlight on Tesla's engineering a few days before the company reports its results.

Fun fact: this isn't the first Roadster to fly. In 2018, SpaceX launched Musk's own red Roadster into space, with a dummy called Starman in the driver's seat. It is still orbiting the Sun.

Based on CBS News, Electrek and CNBC, October 2026.

block.html: Match the word from the text with its meaning. Then use three of them in a sentence about your life.

block.label: QUICK REMINDER · TO OR FOR?
block.html:
To say why (purpose):
• to + verb: Buyers paid $50,000 to reserve a car. (✗ for reserve · ✗ for to reserve)
• for + noun: They went to Texas for the event.
• for + -ing = what a thing is used for: These tanks are for pushing the car into the air.

block.label: PRACTICE · TO OR FOR?
block.html: Choose. Then explain why: is it a verb, a noun or a use?

items.before: We stopped at a gas station

block.label: CONNECTORS · YOUR TOOLBOX FOR LONGER SENTENCES
rows: JOB
CONNECTORS
EXAMPLE
add
and · also · too · as well · besides · moreover · furthermore · in addition · not only… but also
The car is fast. Moreover, it can fly.
contrast
but · however · although · even though · though · despite · in spite of · whereas · while · on the other hand · nevertheless
Despite the delays, people are excited.
cause
because · because of · since · as · due to · thanks to
The event was cancelled due to the weather.
result
so · therefore · as a result · consequently · that's why · so… that
There were six delays. As a result, buyers lost hope.
purpose
to · in order to · so that · for
They paid in order to reserve a car.
condition
if · unless · as long as · provided that · in case
I'll buy one as long as it's safe.
time / sequence
first · then · after that · before · after · while · meanwhile · as soon as · eventually · finally
Eventually, the car appeared.
example
for example · for instance · such as · like
Some cars, such as the Roadster, are mostly for show.
opinion / summary
in my opinion · personally · actually · in fact · in other words · overall · in short
In other words, it's a marketing stunt.
